claims.claim: PM Kisan Samman Nidhi is a Central Sector Scheme providing income support to all landholding farmers' families to supplement their financial needs for procuring agricultural inputs and allied activities as well as domestic needs.
claims.snippet: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) is a new Central Sector Scheme to provide income support to all landholding farmers' families in the country to supplement their financial needs for procuring various inputs related to agriculture and allied activities as well as domestic needs.

claims.claim: The scheme was initially limited to Small and Marginal Farmers with combined landholding up to 2 hectares when launched on 24 February 2019, but was extended to all farmer families irrespective of landholding size effective 1 June 2019.
claims.snippet: In the beginning when the PM-Kisan Scheme was launched on 24th February, 2019, its benefits were admissible only to Small & Marginal Farmers' (SMF) families, with combined landholding upto 2 hectare. The Scheme was later on revised w.e.f. 1.6.2019 and extended to all farmer families irrespective of the size of their landholdings.

claims.claim: All landholding farmers' families which have cultivable landholding in their names are eligible to get benefit under the scheme.
claims.snippet: All landholding farmers' families, which have cultivable landholding in their names are eligible to get benefit under the scheme.

claims.claim: Farmers must own cultivable land in their own name; tenant farmers or those cultivating land owned by others are not eligible.
claims.snippet: No. The land must be in his / her own name. If the land ownership has been transferred in his / her name on account of succession then he / she will be eligible.

claims.claim: Landholding is the sole criterion to avail the benefit under the scheme.
claims.snippet: Land holding is the sole criteria to avail the benefit under the Scheme.

claims.claim: Financial benefit under PM Kisan is Rs. 6,000 per annum per family payable in three equal installments of Rs. 2,000 each every four months.
claims.snippet: Under the PM-KISAN scheme, all landholding farmers' families shall be provided the financial benefit of Rs.6000/- per annum per family payable in three equal installments of Rs.2000/- each, every four months.

claims.claim: The first installment period is 1 December 2018 to 31 March 2019, the second from 1 April 2019 to 31 July 2019, the third from 1 August 2019 to 30 November 2019, and so on.
claims.snippet: The period of 1st installment under the scheme is from 01.12.2018 to 31.03.2019, that of 2nd installment from 01.04.2019 to 31.07.2019, 3rd installment from 01.08.2019 to 30.11.2019, and so on.

claims.claim: Financial benefits under the scheme are directly credited into the bank accounts of beneficiaries.
claims.snippet: Yes. The financial benefit under the scheme shall be directly credited into bank accounts of beneficiaries.

claims.claim: Institutional landholders are not eligible for PM Kisan benefits.
claims.snippet: All Institutional Land holders; and

claims.claim: Former and present holders of constitutional posts, ministers, members of parliament, and mayors of municipal corporations are not eligible for PM Kisan.
claims.snippet: Former and present holders of constitutional posts, Former and present Ministers/ State Ministers and former/present Members of Lok sabha/ Rajya sabha/ state Legislative Assemblies/ State Legislative councils, former and present Mayors of Municipal corporations, former and present Chairpersons of District Panchayats.

claims.claim: All serving or retired officers and employees of Central/State Government Ministries/Offices/Departments, Central or State PSEs, and regular employees of Local Bodies are not eligible for PM Kisan.
claims.snippet: All serving or retired officers and employees of Central/ State Government Ministries /Offices/Departments and its field units Central or State PSEs and Attached offices /Autonomous Institutions under Government as well as regular employees of the Local Bodies are not eligible.

claims.claim: Multi-Tasking Staff (MTS), Class IV, and Group D employees are eligible for PM Kisan provided their families meet other eligibility criteria.
claims.snippet: However serving or retired Multi Tasking Staff / MTS / Class IV / Group D employees are eligible to get benefit under the Scheme, provided their families are otherwise eligible and not covered under other exclusion criteria.

claims.claim: All superannuated or retired pensioners are not eligible for PM Kisan.
claims.snippet: All superannuated/retired pensioners.

claims.claim: All persons who paid income tax in the last assessment year are not eligible for PM Kisan.
claims.snippet: All Persons who paid Income Tax in last assessment year.

claims.claim: Professionals like doctors, engineers, lawyers, chartered accountants, and architects registered with professional bodies are not eligible for PM Kisan.
claims.snippet: Professionals like Doctors, Engineers' Lawyers, Chartered Accountants, and Architects registered with Professional bodies and carrying out profession by undertaking practices.

claims.claim: If any member of a farmer family is an income tax payee in the last assessment year, the entire family is not eligible for PM Kisan.
claims.snippet: No. If an member of the family is income tax payee in last assessment year, then the family is not eligible for benefit under the scheme.

claims.claim: Beneficiaries must provide their bank account details along with Aadhaar number to receive PM Kisan benefits; no benefit can be given without bank account details.
claims.snippet: Yes, the beneficiaries are required to provide their bank account details along with their Aadhaar number so as to credit the financial benefit under the scheme directly into their bank accounts. No benefit can be given if bank account details have not been provided.

claims.claim: Mandatory information required for PM Kisan enrollment includes name, age, gender, category (SC/ST), Aadhaar number (except in Assam, Meghalaya, and J&K until 31 March 2020), bank account number, IFSC code, and mobile number.
claims.snippet: The following information / documents are required to be furnished by the farmers for enrollment under PM-Kisan Scheme: (i) Name, Age, Gender and Category (SC/ST) (ii) Aadhaar Number [except in case of farmers in the States of Assam, Meghalaya and J&K (now UTs of J&K and Laddakh)] (iii) Bank Account Number and IFSC Code (iv) Mobile number.

claims.claim: Farmers can submit their details online through the New Farmer's Registration link in the Farmers Corner on the PM-KISAN portal; the form is forwarded to the State Nodal Officer for verification.
claims.snippet: Through this link, the farmers can submit their details online. The online Form has certain mandatory fields as well self-declaration regarding the eligibility. Once the Form is filled in and submitted successfully by the farmer, the same is forwarded by an automated process to the State Nodal Officer (SNO) for verification.

claims.claim: Eligible beneficiaries whose names are not included in the beneficiary list can approach the District Level Grievance Redressal Monitoring Committee for inclusion or use the New Farmer's Registration link on the PM-KISAN portal.
claims.snippet: All such farmer families whose names are not included in the list of beneficiaries can approach the District Level Grievance Redressal Monitoring Committee in their Districts for inclusion of their names in the beneficiary list. Further, the Government has created an exclusive Farmers' Corner in the PM-KISAN web-portal.

claims.claim: The cutoff date for determination of PM Kisan eligibility is 1 February 2019, and no changes thereafter shall be considered for the next 5 years except for transfer of land through succession due to death.
claims.snippet: The cut-off date for determination of eligibility of beneficiaries under the scheme is 01.02.2019 and no changes thereafter shall be considered for eligibility of benefit under the scheme for next 5 years, except transfer of land on succession in case of death of landholder.

claims.claim: The scheme came into effect from 1 December 2018.
claims.snippet: The scheme takes effect from 01.12.2018.

response.summary:
# PM Kisan Samman Nidhi: Eligibility and Benefits

## Who Can Get PM Kisan

The PM Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) is a central government scheme that provides income support to **all landholding farmer families** across India [1][7]. The core eligibility requirement is straightforward: you must own cultivable land in your own name as per the land records of your state or union territory [1][7].

**Key eligibility criteria:**

- You must be a member of a farmer family (defined as husband, wife, and minor children) that owns cultivable land [7]
- Land ownership must be in your name; tenant farmers or those cultivating land owned by others are not eligible [1]
- Landholding size is irrelevant—the scheme applies to all farmers regardless of how much land they own [1]
- The eligibility cutoff date is 1 February 2019; changes in land ownership after this date are generally not considered for the next 5 years, except in cases of succession due to death [1][7]

## Who Cannot Get PM Kisan

Several categories of people are **excluded** from the scheme, even if they own cultivable land [1][2][7]:

- **Institutional landholders** (such as trusts or cooperatives) [1][7]
- **Government and constitutional office holders**: Former and present holders of constitutional posts, ministers, state ministers, Members of Parliament (Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha), state legislators, mayors of municipal corporations, and district panchayat chairpersons [1][2][7]
- **Government employees**: Serving or retired officers and employees of central/state government ministries, departments, public sector enterprises, and regular employees of local bodies—**with an exception** for Multi-Tasking Staff (MTS), Class IV, and Group D employees, who remain eligible if they meet other criteria [1][2][7]
- **Pensioners**: Superannuated or retired pensioners receiving a monthly pension of ₹10,000 or more (excluding MTS/Class IV/Group D employees) [2][7]
- **Income tax payers**: All persons who paid income tax in the last assessment year; if any family member is an income tax payee, the entire family is ineligible [1][2][7]
- **Professionals**: Doctors, engineers, lawyers, chartered accountants, and architects registered with professional bodies and actively practicing [1][2][7]
- **Non-resident Indians (NRIs)**: As defined under the Income Tax Act, 1961 [7]

## How Much Money Is Given

Under PM-KISAN, eligible farmer families receive **₹6,000 per year** [3][4][6][7]. This amount is disbursed in **three equal installments of ₹2,000 each**, distributed every four months during the financial year [1][6][7]:

- **First installment**: December–March (or April–July in some documentation)
- **Second installment**: April–July (or August–November)
- **Third installment**: August–November (or December–March)

**Payment mechanism:** All funds are transferred directly into beneficiaries' bank accounts through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), requiring the account to be linked with Aadhaar [3][4][6][7].

## Scheme Scale and Recent Disbursements

As of June 2026, the scheme has achieved substantial reach [3][4][8]:

- More than ₹4.46 lakh crore (₹4.46 trillion) has been disbursed through 23 installments since the scheme's launch in February 2019 [3][4][8]
- The 23rd installment (released 20 June 2026) transferred over ₹18,880 crore to more than 9.44 crore farmers, including 2.18 crore women farmers [4][8]
- The Union Cabinet has approved continuation of the scheme from 2026–27 to 2030–31 with a financial outlay of ₹3.15 lakh crore, and the Union Budget 2026–27 allocated ₹60,000 crore for the scheme [3][4]

Women farmers represent approximately 23–25 percent of all beneficiaries [3][4], reflecting the scheme's inclusive outreach.

claims.claim: PM Kisan Samman Nidhi is a Central Sector Scheme providing income support to all landholding farmers' families to supplement their financial needs for procuring agricultural inputs and allied activities as well as domestic needs.
claims.snippet: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) is a new Central Sector Scheme to provide income support to all landholding farmers' families in the country to supplement their financial needs for procuring various inputs related to agriculture and allied activities as well as domestic needs.

claims.claim: The scheme was initially limited to Small and Marginal Farmers with combined landholding up to 2 hectares when launched on 24 February 2019, but was extended to all farmer families irrespective of landholding size effective 1 June 2019.
claims.snippet: In the beginning when the PM-Kisan Scheme was launched on 24th February, 2019, its benefits were admissible only to Small & Marginal Farmers' (SMF) families, with combined landholding upto 2 hectare. The Scheme was later on revised w.e.f. 1.6.2019 and extended to all farmer families irrespective of the size of their landholdings.

claims.claim: All landholding farmers' families which have cultivable landholding in their names are eligible to get benefit under the scheme.
claims.snippet: All landholding farmers' families, which have cultivable landholding in their names are eligible to get benefit under the scheme.

claims.claim: Farmers must own cultivable land in their own name; tenant farmers or those cultivating land owned by others are not eligible.
claims.snippet: No. The land must be in his / her own name. If the land ownership has been transferred in his / her name on account of succession then he / she will be eligible.

claims.claim: Landholding is the sole criterion to avail the benefit under the scheme.
claims.snippet: Land holding is the sole criteria to avail the benefit under the Scheme.

claims.claim: Financial benefit under PM Kisan is Rs. 6,000 per annum per family payable in three equal installments of Rs. 2,000 each every four months.
claims.snippet: Under the PM-KISAN scheme, all landholding farmers' families shall be provided the financial benefit of Rs.6000/- per annum per family payable in three equal installments of Rs.2000/- each, every four months.

claims.claim: The first installment period is 1 December 2018 to 31 March 2019, the second from 1 April 2019 to 31 July 2019, the third from 1 August 2019 to 30 November 2019, and so on.
claims.snippet: The period of 1st installment under the scheme is from 01.12.2018 to 31.03.2019, that of 2nd installment from 01.04.2019 to 31.07.2019, 3rd installment from 01.08.2019 to 30.11.2019, and so on.

claims.claim: Financial benefits under the scheme are directly credited into the bank accounts of beneficiaries.
claims.snippet: Yes. The financial benefit under the scheme shall be directly credited into bank accounts of beneficiaries.

claims.claim: Institutional landholders are not eligible for PM Kisan benefits.
claims.snippet: All Institutional Land holders; and

claims.claim: Former and present holders of constitutional posts, ministers, members of parliament, and mayors of municipal corporations are not eligible for PM Kisan.
claims.snippet: Former and present holders of constitutional posts, Former and present Ministers/ State Ministers and former/present Members of Lok sabha/ Rajya sabha/ state Legislative Assemblies/ State Legislative councils, former and present Mayors of Municipal corporations, former and present Chairpersons of District Panchayats.

claims.claim: All serving or retired officers and employees of Central/State Government Ministries/Offices/Departments, Central or State PSEs, and regular employees of Local Bodies are not eligible for PM Kisan.
claims.snippet: All serving or retired officers and employees of Central/ State Government Ministries /Offices/Departments and its field units Central or State PSEs and Attached offices /Autonomous Institutions under Government as well as regular employees of the Local Bodies are not eligible.

claims.claim: Multi-Tasking Staff (MTS), Class IV, and Group D employees are eligible for PM Kisan provided their families meet other eligibility criteria.
claims.snippet: However serving or retired Multi Tasking Staff / MTS / Class IV / Group D employees are eligible to get benefit under the Scheme, provided their families are otherwise eligible and not covered under other exclusion criteria.

claims.claim: All superannuated or retired pensioners are not eligible for PM Kisan.
claims.snippet: All superannuated/retired pensioners.

claims.claim: All persons who paid income tax in the last assessment year are not eligible for PM Kisan.
claims.snippet: All Persons who paid Income Tax in last assessment year.

claims.claim: Professionals like doctors, engineers, lawyers, chartered accountants, and architects registered with professional bodies are not eligible for PM Kisan.
claims.snippet: Professionals like Doctors, Engineers' Lawyers, Chartered Accountants, and Architects registered with Professional bodies and carrying out profession by undertaking practices.

claims.claim: If any member of a farmer family is an income tax payee in the last assessment year, the entire family is not eligible for PM Kisan.
claims.snippet: No. If an member of the family is income tax payee in last assessment year, then the family is not eligible for benefit under the scheme.

claims.claim: Beneficiaries must provide their bank account details along with Aadhaar number to receive PM Kisan benefits; no benefit can be given without bank account details.
claims.snippet: Yes, the beneficiaries are required to provide their bank account details along with their Aadhaar number so as to credit the financial benefit under the scheme directly into their bank accounts. No benefit can be given if bank account details have not been provided.

claims.claim: Mandatory information required for PM Kisan enrollment includes name, age, gender, category (SC/ST), Aadhaar number (except in Assam, Meghalaya, and J&K until 31 March 2020), bank account number, IFSC code, and mobile number.
claims.snippet: The following information / documents are required to be furnished by the farmers for enrollment under PM-Kisan Scheme: (i) Name, Age, Gender and Category (SC/ST) (ii) Aadhaar Number [except in case of farmers in the States of Assam, Meghalaya and J&K (now UTs of J&K and Laddakh)] (iii) Bank Account Number and IFSC Code (iv) Mobile number.

claims.claim: Farmers can submit their details online through the New Farmer's Registration link in the Farmers Corner on the PM-KISAN portal; the form is forwarded to the State Nodal Officer for verification.
claims.snippet: Through this link, the farmers can submit their details online. The online Form has certain mandatory fields as well self-declaration regarding the eligibility. Once the Form is filled in and submitted successfully by the farmer, the same is forwarded by an automated process to the State Nodal Officer (SNO) for verification.

claims.claim: Eligible beneficiaries whose names are not included in the beneficiary list can approach the District Level Grievance Redressal Monitoring Committee for inclusion or use the New Farmer's Registration link on the PM-KISAN portal.
claims.snippet: All such farmer families whose names are not included in the list of beneficiaries can approach the District Level Grievance Redressal Monitoring Committee in their Districts for inclusion of their names in the beneficiary list. Further, the Government has created an exclusive Farmers' Corner in the PM-KISAN web-portal.

claims.claim: The cutoff date for determination of PM Kisan eligibility is 1 February 2019, and no changes thereafter shall be considered for the next 5 years except for transfer of land through succession due to death.
claims.snippet: The cut-off date for determination of eligibility of beneficiaries under the scheme is 01.02.2019 and no changes thereafter shall be considered for eligibility of benefit under the scheme for next 5 years, except transfer of land on succession in case of death of landholder.

claims.claim: The scheme came into effect from 1 December 2018.
claims.snippet: The scheme takes effect from 01.12.2018.

# PM Kisan Samman Nidhi: Eligibility, Benefits, and Current Status

## Executive Summary

The Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) is India's flagship direct income-support scheme for farmers, providing **₹6,000 per year** (in three installments of ₹2,000 each) directly into the bank accounts of eligible landholding farmer families. The core eligibility criterion is ownership of cultivable land; the scheme excludes higher-income groups, government employees, and certain professionals. As of mid-2026, approximately **9.44–9.49 crore farmers** receive benefits per installment, with total cumulative disbursements exceeding **₹4.47 lakh crore** across 23 installments since inception. The Union Cabinet has approved the scheme's continuation through **2030–31** with a financial outlay of ₹3.15 lakh crore, confirming its long-term operational status.

---

## 1. What Is PM-KISAN?

PM-KISAN is a Central Sector Scheme of the Government of India, implemented by the **Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare**, launched on **February 24, 2019**, and made effective retrospectively from **December 1, 2018** [6]. Its core purpose is to provide income support to landholding farmer families to supplement their financial needs for agricultural inputs (seeds, fertilizers, irrigation, machinery) and domestic expenses [1][7].

When first launched, benefits were limited to Small and Marginal Farmers (SMFs) with landholdings up to 2 hectares. This was revised effective **June 1, 2019**, extending coverage to **all farmer families irrespective of landholding size** [1]. The scheme is structured as a Central Sector scheme, meaning it is fully funded by the Central Government and disbursed directly without state intermediation of funds [7].

---

## 2. Who Is Eligible?

### Core Eligibility Criterion

The eligibility rule is straightforward: **all landholding farmers' families that have cultivable land registered in their names** are eligible [1][7][16]. A "farmer's family" is defined as a unit comprising **husband, wife, and minor children** who collectively own cultivable land as per the land records of the relevant State or Union Territory [7].

> **Landholding is the sole positive criterion.** The scheme imposes no upper limit on the size of the landholding [1].

Practically, benefits are paid only to farmers **whose names appear in land records**. An exception exists for North-East States and Jharkhand, which have different land record structures [7]. Tenant farmers or those cultivating land they do not own are **not eligible** — the land must be in the applicant's own name (or transferred through inheritance/succession) [1].

The eligibility cut-off date is **February 1, 2019**; changes in land ownership after this date are generally not considered for eligibility for the following five years, except in cases of succession due to the death of the landholder [1][7].

---

## 3. Who Is Excluded (Ineligible)?

The scheme applies a set of exclusion criteria based on economic or professional status. If **any member of a farmer family** falls under these categories, the entire family is ineligible [1].

### Full Exclusion Categories

| Category | Details |
|---|---|
| **Institutional landholders** | Any institution (not individuals) that holds land [1][7] |
| **Constitutional post holders** | Former/present holders of constitutional posts [1][2][7] |
| **Elected representatives** | Former/present Ministers, State Ministers, MPs (Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha), MLAs, MLCs, Mayors, District Panchayat Chairpersons [1][2][7] |
| **Government employees** | All serving or retired officers and employees of Central/State Government ministries, departments, field units, PSEs, attached offices, autonomous institutions, and regular employees of local bodies [1][2][7] |
| **Pensioners** | Superannuated/retired pensioners with monthly pension of **₹10,000 or more** [2][7] |
| **Income tax payers** | All persons who paid income tax in the **last assessment year** [1][2][7] |
| **Registered professionals** | Doctors, Engineers, Lawyers, Chartered Accountants, and Architects registered with professional bodies and actively practicing [1][2][7] |
| **Non-Resident Indians (NRIs)** | NRIs as defined under the Income Tax Act, 1961, excluded for new beneficiary registrations [7] |

### Important Exceptions Within Exclusions

- **Multi-Tasking Staff (MTS), Class IV, and Group D government employees** are **exempt from the government-employee exclusion** — they remain eligible provided their families are otherwise not covered by any other exclusion criterion [1][2][7].
- Retired pensioners receiving **less than ₹10,000 per month** are also **not excluded** on grounds of pension alone [2][7].

### Enforcement and Recovery

States and UTs are mandated to conduct recovery proceedings against ineligible beneficiaries. As of **December 2025**, ₹416.75 crore had been recovered from ineligible recipients including income tax payers, government employees, PSU personnel, and constitutional post holders [4][9][16].

---

## 4. How Much Money Is Given and How Is It Disbursed?

### Benefit Amount

- **₹6,000 per year per farmer family** [1][3][6][7]
- Paid in **three equal installments of ₹2,000 each**, covering the following periods [6][7]:
  - **April–July**
  - **August–November**
  - **December–March**

There is **no variation** in the per-family benefit amount based on landholding size, crop type, or region.

### Disbursement Mechanism

Benefits are transferred **directly into farmers' Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts** through the **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)** mechanism [1][4][6][9]. No cash is given; the transfer is electronic and requires:

1. **Land records seeded** in the PM-KISAN portal [4][9]
2. **Bank account linked with Aadhaar** [4][9]
3. **e-KYC completed** [4][9]

The system uses an **Aadhaar-enabled payment system (AePS)** for authentication, ensuring that funds reach the verified beneficiary without intermediaries [6][10].

### Scale of Disbursement

Since inception through 23 installments (as of mid-2026):
- **Total disbursed:** More than **₹4.47 lakh crore** [3][10][14]
- **Women farmers** have received more than **₹1.06 lakh crore**, representing nearly **1 in 4 beneficiaries** [3][10][14]

---

## 5. Current Status in 2026

### Latest Installment (23rd — June 2026)

The **23rd installment** was released on **June 20, 2026**, from Tarakeswar, Hooghly district, West Bengal [8]:
- **Beneficiaries:** Over **9.44–9.49 crore farmers** [4][8][10]
- **Amount disbursed:** Over **₹18,880–₹18,984 crore** [4][8][10]
- **Women beneficiaries:** Over **2.18 crore** [4][8]

Recent installment trend (from official portal data) [11]:

| Installment Period | Beneficiaries |
|---|---|
| APR–JUL 2026–27 (23rd) | 9,44,65,646 |
| DEC–MAR 2025–26 (22nd) | 9,46,15,309 |
| AUG–NOV 2025–26 (21st) | 9,35,79,869 |
| APR–JUL 2025–26 (20th) | 9,71,41,402 |

### Scheme Continuation Approved Through 2030–31

On **July 31, 2026**, the Union Cabinet approved the **continuation of PM-KISAN from 2026–27 to 2030–31**, with a total financial outlay of **₹3.15 lakh crore** [3][10][14]. The Union Budget 2026–27 has separately allocated **₹60,000 crore** for PM-KISAN for the current fiscal year [4][9].

This approval confirms the scheme will run for at least **five more years** beyond its original mandate, locking in annual direct income support for India's farmer families through the next medium-term planning horizon.

---

## 6. How to Apply and What Documents Are Required

### Registration Channels

Farmers can register through three routes [4][15]:
1. **PM-KISAN official portal** (pmkisan.gov.in) — "New Farmer Registration" link in the Farmers' Corner
2. **PM-KISAN Mobile App** (launched February 2020, upgraded with Face Authentication in 2023) [4][15]
3. **Common Service Centres (CSCs)** — over **5 lakh CSCs** have been onboarded [15][16]

After submission, the online form is forwarded to the **State Nodal Officer (SNO)** for eligibility verification [1]. State governments verify land records and upload approved beneficiary details to the central portal [4].

### Mandatory Information Required

| Field | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Name | Farmer's or spouse's name |
| Date of Birth | Farmer's or spouse's date of birth |
| Category | SC/ST status if applicable |
| Aadhaar Number | Mandatory (exceptions existed earlier for Assam, Meghalaya, J&K) |
| Bank Account Number | Required for DBT |
| IFSC/MICR Code | Required for DBT routing |
| Mobile Number | For OTP and communication |
| Other passbook details | As available, for mandate registration |

[1][4][15][16]

### e-KYC Completion

e-KYC is **mandatory** and can be completed via three methods [4][16]:
- **OTP-based authentication** (via mobile number linked to Aadhaar)
- **Biometric authentication** (at CSC or authorized point)
- **Face authentication** (via the PM-KISAN mobile app — no OTP or fingerprint needed)

A unique peer-assistance feature allows one farmer to help up to **100 neighboring farmers** complete e-KYC at their doorstep [15].

### Self-Declaration Requirement

Beneficiaries must submit a **self-declaration** confirming they are not covered by any exclusion category, along with **consent** for the government to use their Aadhaar and other data for eligibility verification with concerned agencies [7][16].

### Grievance Redressal

- Farmers not included in the beneficiary list can approach the **District Level Grievance Redressal Monitoring Committee** [1]
- The **Kisan-eMitra AI chatbot** (launched September 2023) provides 24/7 assistance in **11 Indian languages** (Hindi, English, Tamil, Bengali, Odia, Malayalam, Gujarati, Punjabi, Telugu, Marathi, Kannada) for queries on payments, registration, and eligibility [4][9][15][16]. As of July 2025, it had resolved over **95 lakh queries from 53 lakh farmers** [16].

---

## 7. Impact Evidence (Summary for Decision Context)

Independent evaluations provide corroborating evidence of scheme outcomes:

- **NITI Aayog's DMEO** found that over **92% of beneficiaries** used the assistance for agricultural inputs (seeds, fertilizers, pesticides), and approximately **85% reported improvement in agricultural income** and reduced dependence on informal credit [3][9][13]
- **IFPRI (2019)** found that PM-KISAN helped alleviate short-term credit constraints and enabled increased investment in agricultural inputs [9][13]
- **Kisan Call Centre surveys** found over **92% beneficiary satisfaction** and over **93% utilization for agricultural activities** [9][13]
- A **2022 University of Allahabad study** found paddy yields **3.08% higher** and wheat yields **1.93% higher** on PM-KISAN beneficiary farms vs. non-beneficiary farms [4]
- PM-KISAN covers over **85% of Indian farmers** who own less than two hectares [15][16]

---

## Key Facts at a Glance

| Parameter | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Annual benefit** | ₹6,000 per farmer family |
| **Per installment** | ₹2,000 (three installments/year) |
| **Eligibility** | Cultivable land in farmer's own name |
| **No landholding size cap** | All sizes eligible (since June 1, 2019) |
| **Disbursement mode** | DBT directly into Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts |
| **Current beneficiaries** | ~9.44–9.49 crore per installment (2026) |
| **Cumulative disbursement** | >₹4.47 lakh crore (23 installments) |
| **Latest installment** | 23rd, released June 20, 2026 |
| **Scheme validity** | Approved through 2030–31 |
| **Budget allocation (FY2026–27)** | ₹60,000 crore |
| **Operator** | Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare |

---

*All data sourced from official Government of India sources including the PM-KISAN portal, PIB press releases, Cabinet decisions, and the PM-KISAN Operational Guidelines. Figures current as of the 23rd installment (June 2026) and Cabinet approval (July 31, 2026).*

claims.claim: PM-KISAN is a Central Sector Scheme launched on February 24, 2019, providing annual financial assistance of Rs. 6,000 to each eligible farmer family in three equal instalments of Rs. 2,000 each through Direct Benefit Transfer.
claims.snippet: In order to provide income support to all landholding farmers' families with cultivable land in the country, the Central Government launched the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN), a Central Sector Scheme, on February 24, 2019. The scheme offers annual financial assistance of Rs. 6,000/- to each eligible farmer family, delivered in three equal instalments of Rs. 2,000/-, into their Aadhaar seeded bank accounts of farmers through DBT mode.

claims.claim: All landholding farmers' families who have cultivable land holdings in their names are eligible to receive PM-KISAN benefits.
claims.snippet: All landholding farmers' families, who have cultivable land holdings in their names, are eligible to get benefits under the scheme.

claims.claim: Mandatory information required for PM-KISAN enrollment includes farmer's/spouse's name, date of birth, bank account number, IFSC/MICR code, mobile number, and Aadhaar number.
claims.snippet: Mandatory information required to enroll in the scheme: Farmer's / Spouse's name, Farmer's / Spouse's date of birth, Bank account number, IFSC/ MICR Code, Mobile (contact) Number, Aadhaar Number, Other customer information, available in the passbook, may be required for mandate registration.

claims.claim: The 21st instalment of PM-KISAN will deliver Rs. 18,000 crore to 9 crore farmers through Direct Benefit Transfer.
claims.snippet: 21st instalment delivers ₹18,000 crore to 9 crore farmers through seamless Direct Benefit Transfer.

claims.claim: Over Rs. 3.70 lakh crores have been disbursed to over 11 crore farmer families through 20 instalments since the scheme's launch.
claims.snippet: Over ₹3.70 lakh crore has been disbursed to over 11 crore farmer families since launch, making PM-KISAN one of the world's largest DBT initiatives.

claims.claim: Each instalment of Rs. 2,000 is transferred into farmers' Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts through the Direct Benefit Transfer mode.
claims.snippet: delivered in three equal instalments of Rs. 2,000/-, into their Aadhaar seeded bank accounts of farmers through DBT mode.

claims.claim: Ineligible categories for PM-KISAN include individuals belonging to higher-income groups, income tax payees, employees of PSUs, State/Central Government employees, and Constitutional post holders.
claims.snippet: States/UTs have been mandated to recover funds disbursed to ineligible farmers such as individuals belonging to higher-income groups, income tax payees, employees of PSUs, State/Central Govt., Constitutional post holders etc.

claims.claim: As of August 5, 2025, a total of Rs. 416 crore has been recovered from ineligible recipients across the country.
claims.snippet: As of 5 August 2025, a total of Rs. 416 crore has been recovered from ineligible recipients across the country.

claims.claim: Beneficiaries must submit a self-declaration confirming they are not excluded under the scheme's eligibility criteria and must consent to the government using their Aadhaar and other information for verification purposes.
claims.snippet: Beneficiaries are required to submit a self-declaration confirming that they are not excluded under the scheme's eligibility criteria. This declaration must include the beneficiary's consent for the government to use their Aadhaar and other information for verification purposes.

claims.claim: PM-KISAN is one of the world's largest Direct Benefit Transfer initiatives globally.
claims.snippet: This scheme stands out as one of the largest Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) initiative globally, underscoring its monumental impact on facilitating financial support directly to the beneficiaries.

claims.claim: Over 25% of PM-KISAN benefits are dedicated to women beneficiaries.
claims.snippet: With a commitment to inclusivity, it dedicates over 25% of its benefits to women beneficiaries.

claims.claim: Farmers can complete e-KYC through OTP-based, biometric-based, or face authentication-based options.
claims.snippet: Now farmers can complete their e-KYC by using any following option: OTP based e-KYC, Biometric-based e-KYC, Face authentication-based e-KYC.

claims.snippet: Over 5 lakh Common Service Centres (CSCs) have been onboarded to facilitate registrations and meet mandatory requirements.
